245:### Design Decision and spec review
246-
247-- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
248-  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
249-  the issue body.
250-- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
251-  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
252-  comment must say what was checked:
253-  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
254-  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
255-  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;

270-
271-Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
272-`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:
273-
274-1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and

276-2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
277-3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
278-4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
279-   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

293-   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
294-     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
295-   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`

349-## Mutation testing (D6)
350-
351-A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
352-or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
353-**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
354-to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
355-test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.
356-
357-**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
358-small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.
359-
360-| Code changed | Tool |
361-| --- | --- |
362-| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
363-| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |
364-
365-1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
366-   project.
367-2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
368-   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
369-3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
370-   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
371-   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
372-4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.
373-
374-Files:
375-
376-- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, using the template below.
377-- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
378-  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<github-username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
379-  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`.
380-  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
381-  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
382-- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
383-  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
384-  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.
385-
386-Common problems:
387-
388-- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
389-  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
390-- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
391-  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
392-- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
393-  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
394-- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated

When posting a one-sentence review, such as an Approve after a requested fix lands, write just the sentence, with no AI disclaimer or attribution line.

**Why:** On 2026-10-06, when approving PR #72, the user said "do NOT put ai disclaimers, it's one sentence".
On 2026-10-18 the user also dropped the AI line from the `Spec reviewed — ...` comments on #56, #58 and #59 ("you don't need to put an ai disclaimer"). Spec-review comments stay bare too.

**How to apply:** Keep the AI-assistance line for the full code-review rubric comment (see [[commit-and-pr-conventions]]). Short approvals and follow-ups stay bare. The session's AI log and the #55-style issue comment still cover the AI use.

Source: `https://csci-435-se.github.io/sprint3/`, `/ai-logs/` and `/glossary/`, fetched 2026-11-04. No page shows an edit date, so re-fetch before relying on a line here. Each sprint page only lists changes; anything it leaves out falls back to earlier sprint pages.

**Sprint 3: Nov 3 to Nov 19, 100 points (12% of course).**
- **Deadlines:** D7 check-in plus at least one code PR you authored (open and ready, or merged) due **Nov 12, 11:59 PM**. Everything else, including the D10 survey, due **Nov 19, 11:59 PM**. No late policy stated (syllabus: 2-hour grace, then 10% per day).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no report (D8) or no release (D9) gives the team 0 for the sprint.
- **Points:** D1 backlog 10 (team), D2 spec 20, D3 design 5, D4 PRs 20 (averaged, scaled to 20), D5 AI logs 5, D6 mutation 15, D7 check-in 5, D8 report 10 (team), D9 release 2 (team), D10 reflection survey 8 (link via Blackboard/Zulip near sprint end).
- **Graded strictly:** code PR open by the check-in; merge only after a teammate approves the **latest commit**; spec review comment on the issue saying what was checked (each AC clear and testable, cases and whether ACs cover them, scope fit), "Looks good!" alone is not acceptable; `Closes #N` plus issue and PR on the `Sprint 3` milestone; real AI logs; report renders (no escaped `\|` or `\[`).
- **D1 load:** CSCI 435 = at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent points); one assignee per issue; each issue states small/medium scope with 1-2 sentences why (TA may reclassify). Sprint 2 carryovers go in first or are dropped with a reason on the issue. Optional: one issue may be a hardening issue. The instructor/TA posts a Sprints 3-4 team feature as an issue; its sub-issues (owner, spec, scope, linked, on milestone) count toward load. It is #20 (posted by 2026-11-07; sub-issues #143-145, all ab-wm's).
- **Hardening evidence:** bug fix = failing-then-passing test; flaky = root cause plus 20 unit / 10 E2E runs before and after; CI check = run links before and after; baseline failures = counts before and after with causes. Reformatting, regenerating snapshots or silencing a check counts as small at most.
- **D2/D3:** spec reviewed before coding; each design decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won (issue body, issue comment or PR all count).
- **D4 PRs:** `## Test Evidence` table `Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value`, one row per AC; levels unit/integration/E2E/manual; sources AC, issue discussion, docs, upstream behavior, other; "the current output of your own code is not a valid source". Plus `**Not tested automatically, and why:**` and `**AI-written tests:**` ("None." if none). `## Tech Debt` with `**Introduced:**` and `**Encountered:**` ("None." valid). Rubric: ACs 6, tests and Test Evidence 6, description/Tech Debt/issue link 3, CI or documented manual checks 3, rubric review and approval on latest commit 2. Reviewers respond within 24 hours.
- **D6 mutation testing:** one issue whose PR changes source and tests; a tool is required (StrykerJS + Vitest runner for frontend, Gremlins or go-mutesting for Go; the team chose go-mutesting, see `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`). Run only on the PR's changed files. Analyse every survivor (at least 10 if more), add a test that kills a gap survivor and re-run. Files: `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<user>.md` and `reports/<issue#>-<user>-{before,after}.json` (`.txt` for go-mutesting). Rubric: run and reports 4, survivors 4, killing test 4, answers 3. Blockers go to the TA early.
- **D7 check-in:** `docs/sprint3/checkin/<user>.md`, about 100 words each on: done and remaining; one thing learned about testing; one risk and the plan. On time with a PR linked = 5; late, thin or no PR = 3; missing = 0.
- **D8 report:** Sprint 1 sections plus Suite health (baseline at tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` and at sprint end, failures grouped by cause with one issue each, no new failures, skipped tests need an issue and a code comment), links to D6 files, hardening issues, carryovers.
- **D9:** tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s3` after the last merge, plus a GitHub release summarising features, fixes and hardening.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 per upstream PR accepted or under active review, up to 2 per upstream bug confirmed by Sprint 4 grading.

**AI logs (all sprints):** `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<slug>.md` (tool id e.g. `claude-code`), attachments in a same-named folder, `.md`/`.txt`/`.json` only. Full prompts and output; summaries, paraphrases, share links or output without prompts don't count. One AI Assistance comment per contributor per issue worked, linking the log file itself, or "No AI used." Unproductive sessions get logged too.

**Carried from Sprints 1-2:** no self-approval or self-merge; each student reviews at least one PR per sprint; branch deleted after merge.

**Reading the rules:** the course site wins over `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`. Where the repo doc is stricter (D3 in the issue body only, the exact `Spec reviewed` opener), present it as team convention, not a grading risk. A missing design section at spec review is a reminder, never a blocker.

**Why:** I twice over-read the design rule from the repo doc instead of the site (#55 in Sprint 1; #56/#58/#59 spec reviews on 2026-10-18). PR #94's rewrite of the course rules also missed site rules until CodeRabbit flagged them.
**How to apply:** Quote the site before flagging a deliverable problem. When a new sprint starts, re-fetch and rewrite this file. See [[sprint-history]], [[ai-log-tooling]].

```text
Closes #144

## What changed and why

Since #143, a pull request whose dependencies are not done cannot be merged, but its page did not say so: the merge button was still offered and only failed once pressed, and in the sidebar a merged pull request looked the same as one closed without merging. This PR makes the page say which dependencies block the merge, offers no merge while they do, and shows each dependency's state.

- **The merge box names what blocks the merge (AC1, AC4, AC6).** It shows "This pull request is blocked by its dependencies:" with a link to each one, written as the timeline writes a dependency: `#N title` in the same repository, `owner/repo#N - title` in another. A dependency the viewer cannot read is only counted, with the sidebar's existing "You do not have permission to read 1 dependency". The list uses the very rule #143's merge check uses, so the page and the check cannot disagree (Decision 1). With dependencies turned off, nothing is shown.
- **No merge is offered while blocked (AC2).** The merge buttons, their "(When checks succeed)" form and the "This pull request can be merged automatically." line are gone while dependencies block. "Manually merged", which #143 leaves unblocked, stays where the repository allows it, for anyone who could merge the pull request right now; someone held back by branch protection gets no merge form at all, as it would otherwise open as "Manually merged (When checks succeed)" (Decision 2).
- **A scheduled merge can still be cancelled while blocked (Decision 3).** If a merge was scheduled for "when checks succeed" before a dependency blocked it, the merge box keeps the schedule's notice and its "Cancel auto merge" button, without offering a way to merge. A pull request with conflicts gets that Cancel button back too, which `main` lacked.
- **Nothing changes when nothing blocks (AC3).** A pull request with no dependencies, or only closed issues and merged pull requests, gets the same merge box as before.
- **The sidebar shows each dependency's state (AC5).** Every entry in "Depends on" and "Blocks" gets Gitea's usual state icon and its state, "Open", "Closed" or "Merged", after the repository name, so a merged pull request no longer looks like a closed one.
- The docs in `.claude-students` describe how the merge box is built and why a blocker nobody can override has to remove the merge styles, the rule the merge box shares with the merge check, and how a handler test reads English text instead of locale keys.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** A pull request with an open issue, a pull request closed without merging, and an issue in another repository as dependencies shows the message and one link per dependency; a closed issue and a merged pull request are not listed.
- **AC2:** While blocked, a user who can merge sees only "Manually merged" where the repository allows it, and no merge form where it does not or where branch protection holds them back.
- **AC3:** Without dependencies, or once they are resolved, the merge box offers the same styles and lines as before, including for a pull request with conflicts and for a viewer who cannot merge yet.
- **AC4:** A blocking dependency the viewer cannot read is counted, without its title, whether or not readable ones are listed with it.
- **AC5:** Each "Depends on" and "Blocks" entry shows "Open", "Closed", or "Merged" for a merged pull request.
- **AC6:** With dependencies turned off, neither the merge box nor the sidebar shows any.

## CI / manual verification

- CI runs on the PR and must pass before merging, per course rules.
- Claude ran this branch on a local instance, with a headless browser and the API, to check the merge box's message and links, which merge options it offers with "Manually merged" on and off and under a protection rule, the merge button coming back once a dependency is closed, and the sidebar's states.
- I checked the changes on an instance, ensuring that feedback actually exists for the new blocking rule, unlike before where #143 only gave feedback once Merge was pressed. Additionally, ensured that "Manually merged" shows in the UI as the only option while blocked, where the repository allows it.

## Design

Design decisions noted under issue #144.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- A pull request page now looks up the viewer's permissions for its dependencies twice, once for the sidebar and once for the merge box. The merge box also reloads on its own, without the sidebar's data, so it does its own lookup.

**Encountered:**
- The merge form opens a lone merge style in "(When checks succeed)" mode for someone who cannot merge right now. On `main` a conflicted pull request already shows "Manually merged (When checks succeed)". This PR avoids it for blocked pull requests (Decision 2) and leaves the conflicted case alone, as outside #144.
- Gitea's existing merge-box code has few Go unit tests: the mutation run left 184 survivors in the unchanged code of the functions this PR touched. Only the cases this PR's ACs need were added.
```

```text
+// GetMergeBlockingDependencies returns the dependencies that block merging pr, each with its repository loaded.
+func GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (issueDeps []*DependencyInfo, err error) {
+	err = db.GetEngine(ctx).
+		Table("issue").
+		Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = issue.repo_id").
+		Join("INNER", "issue_dependency", "issue_dependency.dependency_id = issue.id").
+		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
+		And(mergeBlockingDependencyCond()).
+		Find(&issueDeps)
+
+	for _, depInfo := range issueDeps {
+		depInfo.Issue.Repo = &depInfo.Repository
+	}
+
+	return issueDeps, err
+}
+
+// mergeBlockingDependencyCond matches an open issue or pull request, or a pull request closed without merging.
+// Shared so the merge check and the merge box list the same dependencies.
+func mergeBlockingDependencyCond() builder.Cond {
+	return builder.Or(
+		builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
+		builder.In("issue.id", builder.Select("issue_id").From("pull_request").Where(builder.Eq{"has_merged": false})),
+	)
+}

+// prepareMergeBoxDependencies lists the dependencies that block merging, the same ones the merge check refuses.
+func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxDependencies(ctx *context.Context) {
+	if !ctx.Repo.Repository.IsDependenciesEnabled(ctx) {
+		return
+	}
+	deps, err := issues_model.GetMergeBlockingDependencies(ctx, prInfo.issue.PullRequest)
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("GetMergeBlockingDependencies", err)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(deps) == 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.isBlockedByDependencies = true
+	canRead, notPermitted := checkBlockedByIssues(ctx, deps)
+	if ctx.Written() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	items := make([]template.HTML, 0, len(canRead)+1)
+	for _, dep := range canRead {
+		// as the timeline shows a dependency: the repository only when it is another one
+		if dep.Issue.RepoID == prInfo.issue.RepoID {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">#%d %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		} else {
+			items = append(items, htmlutil.HTMLFormat(`<a href="%s">%s#%d - %s</a>`, dep.Issue.Link(), dep.Issue.Repo.FullName(), dep.Issue.Index, dep.Issue.Title))
+		}
+	}
+	if len(notPermitted) > 0 {
+		items = append(items, ctx.Locale.TrN(len(notPermitted), "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_1", "repo.issues.dependency.no_permission_n", len(notPermitted)))
+	}
+	prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.blocked_by_dependencies"), items)
+}
```

```text
func (c *pullMergeBoxInfoItemCollection) AddErrorItem(info template.HTML, optItems ...[]template.HTML) {
	c.items = append(c.items, &pullMergeBoxInfoItem{
		SvgIconHTML: svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x", 16, "tw-text-red"),
		InfoHTML:    info,
		ListItems:   util.OptionalArg(optItems),
	})
}

func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxIconColor() {
	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	mergeBoxData := prInfo.MergeBoxData

	showAsNormalColor := prInfo.issue.IsClosed || prInfo.workInProgressPrefix != "" || pull.IsEmpty() || pull.IsFilesConflicted()
	showAsErrorColor := false
	showAsWarningColor := pull.IsChecking()

	if statusCheckData := mergeBoxData.StatusCheckData; statusCheckData != nil {
		showAsErrorColor = statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsError() || statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsFailure() ||
			statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsError() || statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsFailure()

		showAsWarningColor = showAsWarningColor ||
			statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsWarning() || statusCheckData.pullCommitStatusState.IsPending() ||
			((mergeBoxData.enableStatusCheck || mergeBoxData.hasRequiredStatusContexts) && (statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsWarning() || statusCheckData.RequiredChecksState.IsPending()))
	}

	hasBlockers := len(mergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.items) > 0 || len(mergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.items) > 0

	switch {
	case pull.HasMerged:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-purple"
	case showAsNormalColor:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-text-light"
	case showAsErrorColor:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-red"
	case showAsWarningColor:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-yellow"
	case hasBlockers:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-red"
	case pull.IsStatusMergeable():
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-green"
	default:
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.TimelineIconClass = "tw-text-text-light"
	}
}

<script lang="ts" setup>
import {computed, onMounted, onUnmounted, shallowRef, watch} from 'vue';
import {SvgIcon} from '../svg.ts';
import {toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const props = defineProps<{
  mergeFormProps: any, // TODO: this is a huge object, need to be refactored in the future
}>();

const mergeStyleManuallyMerged = 'manually-merged';

const mergeForm = props.mergeFormProps;

const mergeTitleFieldValue = shallowRef('');
const mergeMessageFieldValue = shallowRef('');
const deleteBranchAfterMerge = shallowRef(false);
const autoMergeWhenSucceed = shallowRef(false);

const mergeStyle = shallowRef('');
const mergeStyleDetail = shallowRef({
  hideMergeMessageTexts: false,
  textDoMerge: '',
  mergeTitleFieldText: '',
  mergeMessageFieldText: '',
  hideAutoMerge: false,
});

const mergeStyleAllowedCount = shallowRef(0);
// with no style to offer, the form only shows a scheduled merge's notice and cancel button
const hasAllowedMergeStyle = mergeForm.mergeStyles.some((e: any) => e.allowed);

const showMergeStyleMenu = shallowRef(false);
const showActionForm = shallowRef(false);

const mergeButtonStyleClass = computed(() => {
  if (mergeStyle.value === mergeStyleManuallyMerged) return 'red';
  if (mergeForm.allOverridableChecksOk) return 'primary';
  return autoMergeWhenSucceed.value ? 'primary' : 'red';
});

const mergeSelectStyleClass = computed(() => {
  if (mergeForm.emptyCommit) return '';
  if (mergeStyle.value === mergeStyleManuallyMerged) return 'red';
  return 'primary';
});

const forceMerge = computed(() => {
  return mergeForm.canMergeNow && !mergeForm.allOverridableChecksOk;
});

watch(mergeStyle, (val) => {
  mergeStyleDetail.value = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.name === val);
  for (const elem of document.querySelectorAll('[data-pull-merge-style]')) {
    toggleElem(elem, elem.getAttribute('data-pull-merge-style') === val);
  }
});

onMounted(() => {
  mergeStyleAllowedCount.value = mergeForm.mergeStyles.reduce((v: any, msd: any) => v + (msd.allowed ? 1 : 0), 0);

  let mergeStyle = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.allowed && e.name === mergeForm.defaultMergeStyle)?.name;
  if (!mergeStyle) mergeStyle = mergeForm.mergeStyles.find((e: any) => e.allowed)?.name;
  switchMergeStyle(mergeStyle, !mergeForm.canMergeNow);

  document.addEventListener('mouseup', hideMergeStyleMenu);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  document.removeEventListener('mouseup', hideMergeStyleMenu);
});

function hideMergeStyleMenu() {
  showMergeStyleMenu.value = false;
}

function toggleActionForm(show: boolean) {
  showActionForm.value = show;
  if (!show) return;
  deleteBranchAfterMerge.value = mergeForm.defaultDeleteBranchAfterMerge;
  mergeTitleFieldValue.value = mergeStyleDetail.value.mergeTitleFieldText;
  mergeMessageFieldValue.value = mergeStyleDetail.value.mergeMessageFieldText;
}

function switchMergeStyle(name: string, autoMerge = false) {
  mergeStyle.value = name;
  autoMergeWhenSucceed.value = autoMerge;
}

function clearMergeMessage() {
  mergeMessageFieldValue.value = mergeForm.defaultMergeMessage;
}
</script>
```

```text
func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) preparePullUpdateActions(ctx *context.Context) {
	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	data := prInfo.MergeBoxData
	userUpdateStyles, err := pull_service.CheckUserAllowedToUpdate(ctx, pull, ctx.Doer)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("IsUserAllowedToUpdate", err)
		return
	}
	if !userUpdateStyles.MergeAllowed && !userUpdateStyles.RebaseAllowed {
		return
	}

	issueLink := prInfo.issue.Link()
	mergeAction := &pullUpdateAction{
		URL:  issueLink + "/update?style=merge",

				if errForceMerge != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule failed, repo: %v, base branch: %v, err: %w", pr.BaseRepoID, pr.BaseBranch, errForceMerge)
				}

				canForceMerge := isRepoAdmin
				if protectedBranchRule != nil {
					canForceMerge = git_model.CanBypassBranchProtection(ctx, protectedBranchRule, doer, isRepoAdmin)
				}
				if canForceMerge {
					errProtection = nil
				}
			}

			// If there is still a branch protection check error, return it
			if errProtection != nil {
				return errProtection
			}
		}

		if err := checkSigningRequirements(ctx, pr, doer, mergeStyle); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if pr.BaseRepo.IsDependenciesEnabled(ctx) { // closing skips dependencies too when they are turned off
			if blocked, err := issues_model.MergeBlockedByDependencies(ctx, pr); err != nil {
				return err
			} else if blocked {
				return ErrDependenciesLeft
			}
		}

		return nil
	})
}

// checkSigningRequirements enforces the target branch's RequireSignedCommits rule
// against the selected merge style:

//     those commits must all be verified, or the pre-receive hook will reject the
//     push with a generic error.
//   - fast-forward-only creates no Gitea commit, so Gitea's signing key is not used.
//   - merge, rebase, rebase-merge and squash produce a Gitea-signed commit, so
//     Gitea must be configured to sign it.
```

```text
func (prInfo *pullRequestViewInfo) prepareMergeBoxInfoItems(ctx *context.Context) {
	pull := prInfo.issue.PullRequest
	data := prInfo.MergeBoxData

	if pull.HasMerged && data.IsPullBranchDeletable {
		data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_success")
		data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.merged_info_text", htmlutil.HTMLFormat("<code>%s</code>", prInfo.headTarget))
		return
	} else if prInfo.issue.IsClosed {
		data.ClosedInfoTitle = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.closed")
		if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
			data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cant_reopen_deleted_branch")
		} else {
			data.ClosedInfoBody = ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.reopen_to_merge")
		}
		return
	}

	if pull.IsFilesConflicted() {
		detailItems := escapeStringSliceToHTML(pull.ConflictedFiles)
		if len(detailItems) == 0 {
			detailItems = append(detailItems, ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted_no_listed_files"))
		}
		if len(detailItems) > 10 {
			detailItems = detailItems[:10]
			detailItems = append(detailItems, "...")
		}
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.files_conflicted"),
			detailItems,
		)
	}

	if prInfo.IsPullRequestBroken {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-x"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.data_broken"),
		)
	}

	if pull.IsChecking() {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("gitea-running", 16, "rotate-clockwise"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_checking"),
		)
	}

	if pull.IsAncestor() {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoCommitBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_ancestor"),
		)
	}

	if !pull.IsStatusMergeable() {
		// it is only a "protection" level blocker, it can be bypassed by admin (e.g.: manually merged)
		if pull.IsEmpty() {
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-alert"),
				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.is_empty"),
			)
		} else {
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddErrorItem(ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_desc"))
			prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
				svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
				ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.cannot_auto_merge_helper"),
			)
		}
	}

	if !data.hasPermToMerge {
		prInfo.MergeBoxData.infoProtectionBlockers.AddInfoItem(
			svg.RenderHTML("octicon-info"),
			ctx.Locale.Tr("repo.pulls.no_merge_access"),
		)
	}
```
